Consent

By answering the following questions, you are participating in a study being performed by cognitive scientists in the Stanford Department of Psychology. If you have questions about this research, please contact us at stanfordpsych251@gmail.com. You must be at least 18 years old to participate. Your participation in this research is voluntary. You may decline to answer any or all of the following questions. You may decline further participation, at any time, without adverse consequences. Your anonymity is assured; the researchers who have requested your participation will not receive any personal information about you.

During this experiment, you will hear different tone sequences. Listen carefully to each one. Pay attention to which sequences are common and which are rare.

Debrief

Thank you. This study tests whether hearing an unexpected sound changes the decisions people make. Most choices followed the common tone sequence, and some followed a rare one. The tones had no connection to the gambles: every gamble was a true 50/50 chance, whatever you heard. The points did not affect your payment. The mood questions were included because the original study asked them; they are not a diagnosis.

If you have questions about this research, contact stanfordpsych251@gmail.com. Press the button to save your responses and finish.
